pages.title: Project & setup
pages.summary: Build, test, and understand the correctness-first CKKS GPU project.
takeaways: Start with the CPU build and exactness tests; no CUDA device is needed.
CUDA accelerates the NTT baseline. Base conversion, Hybrid key switching and OpenFHE integration are later milestones.

pages.title: NTT & butterflies
pages.summary: Direct sums, recursive butterflies, handwritten derivations, and an interactive stage/twiddle calculator.
takeaways: The NTT evaluates a polynomial at roots of unity; butterflies reuse smaller sums.
Negacyclic evaluation uses odd powers of the primitive 2N-th root. Open the lesson to try the twiddle and stage controls.

pages.title: From CPU to CUDA
pages.summary: Threads, blocks, shared memory, and this repository's two-pass GPU schedule.
takeaways: A block cooperates on one strided group or contiguous tile; its threads share the local butterfly work.
The two passes reorganize the same NTT stages without changing the output order.

pages.title: 65536: work distribution
pages.summary: Explore the 65536-point forward/inverse polynomial, two-pass blocks, threads, and global access patterns.
takeaways: At N=65,536, the forward transform uses eight strided and eight contiguous stages.
Inverse reverses the pass order and finishes with normalization. Use the explorer to follow one block and thread.

pages.title: CUDA buffers & dataflow
pages.summary: D5: constructor lifecycle, buffer ownership, host/device copies, fused operations, and integration gaps.
takeaways: Host-facing calls validate, upload, launch and download.
The fused ring product keeps its intermediate arrays on the device, avoiding repeated host roundtrips.

pages.title: Arithmetic bounds & tests
pages.summary: D6: canonical residues, overflow proofs, bigint checks, full-size adversarial cases, and remaining exactness gates.
takeaways: Keep residues canonical and prove overflow bounds before changing a reduction routine.
Check arithmetic against a bigint oracle and compare transforms exactly.

pages.title: OpenFHE representation
pages.summary: D7: exact coefficient/evaluation ordering, root selection, DCRT tower packing, format APIs, and executable compatibility checks.
takeaways: Match OpenFHE’s roots, tower order and evaluation layout, not just roundtrip behavior.
Compare coefficient and evaluation arrays residue by residue.

pages.title: Hybrid operation graph
pages.summary: D8: exact digit extension, Q/P tower addressing, key MAC, ModDown, delayed operations, and full-size OpenFHE checks.
takeaways: Hybrid key switching extends digits to QP, accumulates key products and reduces back to Q.
This page documents the operation graph and CPU checks, not a completed GPU key-switch implementation.

pages.title: Device backend contract
pages.summary: D9: checked buffer views, stream dependencies, resource leases, cache identities, and the proposed OpenFHE adapter.
takeaways: Device buffers need explicit format, basis, ownership and ordering rules.
Use the same exactness contract across the adapter and its fallback.

pages.title: Resident operation chain
pages.summary: A bounded single-stream prototype: owned handles, queued dependencies, exact OpenFHE host checks, failure quarantine and compiled CUDA transport.
takeaways: Upload once, queue transforms and multiplication, then download the result.
Host and compiler checks do not establish native execution or performance for the new resident path.

pages.title: Run & debug
pages.summary: Run the N=8 example and step through each butterfly in VS Code.
takeaways: Start with the N=8 debug example and step through one butterfly.
Use the existing VS Code launch configuration; the full instructions are below.

pages.title: GPU NTT implementations
pages.summary: Primary-source survey, performance limits, and techniques to evaluate.
takeaways: Prioritize reducing data movement and test arithmetic and layout changes independently.
Compare candidates under the same inputs, timing scope and correctness checks.

pages.title: Choosing the GPU
pages.summary: Compare hardware for exact u32/u64 modular arithmetic and CKKS workloads.
takeaways: Select hardware for integer modular arithmetic, memory behavior and profiling access.
RTX 5090 is the target; the temporary Ada run does not rank it against other GPUs.

pages.title: GPU rental market
pages.summary: November 2026 provider comparison, verified public rates, a live offer sample, session budgets and CUDA profiling access.
takeaways: Verify the rental’s device, CUDA toolkit and profiler permissions before starting paid work.
Treat recorded prices and offers as dated evidence, not current availability.

pages.title: Integration roadmap
pages.summary: The tracked 95-working-day plan through exact OpenFHE Hybrid integration.
takeaways: The sequence is NTT → base conversion → Hybrid key switching → OpenFHE integration.
Keep the temporary Ada baseline separate from the pending RTX 5090 acceptance gate.

pages.title: Architecture decision
pages.summary: D10: accepted representation, backend ownership, adapter/fallback policy, resource budgets and P1 review.
takeaways: Match OpenFHE’s representation exactly and keep a CPU fallback.
Keep device ownership and synchronization explicit across the adapter.

pages.title: Implementation backlog
pages.summary: D10: dependency-ordered native GPU, resident runtime, cache, conversion, Hybrid and adapter acceptance gates.
takeaways: Work through verification, residency, conversion, key switching and integration in dependency order.
Use the full checklist when accepting an implementation milestone.

pages.title: Before renting a GPU
pages.summary: Completed compiler-only preparation, baseline safety fixes, tested session reporting and the first real-GPU handoff.
takeaways: Build and verify what you can offline; use rented time for native CUDA checks and timings.
Confirm exactness, sanitizers and profiling access before collecting performance data.

pages.title: Benchmarks & tuning
pages.summary: Workload matrix, profiling evidence, and per-device kernel selection.
takeaways: Benchmark dimensions 4,096–65,536, up to 40 prime towers and 30/50/55/60-bit primes.
Keep public-call, resident-device, transfer and CPU timing scopes separate.

pages.title: First GPU run: analysis
pages.summary: Saved native evidence, exactness scope, benchmark caveats, transfer accounting, bottleneck hypotheses and next offline experiments.
takeaways: The first native run established exactness on the tested temporary GPU cases.
Its limited timing sample could not isolate kernel arithmetic from transfer and wrapper costs.

pages.title: Full GPU matrix: analysis
pages.summary: 140-workload results through 40 primes: exactness, public versus resident timings, fusion, transfers, 30-bit behavior and the separate M1 Pro baseline.
takeaways: Fused polynomial multiplication beat the unfused chain in all 140 workloads (2.36× median ratio).
Results are from the temporary GPU and a separate M1 Pro CPU baseline, not RTX 5090 or end-to-end CKKS measurements.

pages.title: Offline test tooling
pages.summary: Raw timing samples, strict report validation and shared constructor ownership tests prepared for the next native GPU session.
takeaways: Run GPU timings on the rental and CPU timings locally.
Keep fixed inputs, validated raw samples and separate platform provenance.

pages.title: Writing & publishing
pages.summary: Preview the site, add a daily journal entry, and publish the HTML documentation.
takeaways: Edit source documents, then rebuild and validate links before publishing.
Record dated engineering outcomes in the journal; keep generated HTML out of the source workflow.
